knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. A divisibility rule. NCERT Class 6 states the test; the Class 8 outcome (LO-M803) asks for its proof. Kind has two readings (Principle, because it states what is true of every whole number, or Procedure, because it is used as a test); recorded as Principle.

knowledge_items.statement: A whole number is divisible by 11 exactly when the difference between the sum of its digits in the odd places and the sum of its digits in the even places, counted from the right, is 0 or divisible by 11.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. A divisibility rule. NCERT Class 6 states the test; the Class 8 outcome (LO-M803) asks for its proof. Kind has two readings (Principle, because it states what is true of every whole number, or Procedure, because it is used as a test); recorded as Principle.

knowledge_items.statement: A prime number is a whole number greater than 1 whose only factors are 1 and itself.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: Every whole number greater than 1 can be written as a product of prime numbers, and the primes in the product are the same for every way of writing it, apart from their order.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: To write a number as a product of primes, divide it by a prime that divides it, repeat on each quotient until the quotient is 1, and write the divisors as a product.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. A factor tree gives the same result; it is a way of recording the same procedure.

knowledge_items.statement: A whole number is a perfect square exactly when every prime occurs an even number of times in its prime factorisation, so that its prime factors can be grouped in pairs of equal primes with none left over.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: A whole number is a perfect cube exactly when every prime occurs a multiple of three times in its prime factorisation, so that its prime factors can be grouped in triples of equal primes with none left over.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: To find the square root of a perfect square by prime factorisation, write its prime factorisation, group equal primes in pairs, and multiply one prime from each pair.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: To find the cube root of a perfect cube by prime factorisation, write its prime factorisation, group equal primes in triples, and multiply one prime from each triple.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n².
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: To find the square root of a perfect square by repeated subtraction, subtract the odd numbers 1, 3, 5, … in order from the number until the result is 0; the number of subtractions is the square root.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: To find the square root of a whole number by the division method, group its digits in pairs from the right; take as the first digit of the root the largest digit whose square is not more than the first group, subtract, bring down the next pair, and choose each next digit so that the new divisor, which is twice the root so far followed by that digit, multiplied by that digit is not more than the remainder; repeat until no pairs are left.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT Class 8 does not justify the procedure, so the rationale label is without.

knowledge_items.statement: To find the square root of a decimal by the division method, group the digits of the whole-number part in pairs leftwards from the decimal point and the digits of the decimal part in pairs rightwards, adding a zero to complete the last pair, divide as for a whole number, and write the decimal point in the root when the first pair after the decimal point is brought down.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: When the division method for a whole number leaves a non-zero remainder after the last pair, write a decimal point after the root and continue by bringing down pairs of zeros; each further pair of zeros gives one more decimal place of an approximate root.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: To find the smallest number by which a number must be multiplied, or divided, to make a perfect square, write its prime factorisation and take the product of the primes that occur an odd number of times.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The same product is the smallest multiplier and the smallest divisor.

knowledge_items.statement: To find the smallest number by which a number must be divided to make a perfect cube, write its prime factorisation, group equal primes in triples, and divide by the product of the primes left over; to find the smallest number by which it must be multiplied, multiply by the primes needed to complete each incomplete triple.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: If a whole number is greater than n² and less than (n + 1)², its square root is greater than n and less than n + 1.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: For a number a and a whole number n greater than 1, a^n is a multiplied by itself n times, where a is the base and n is the exponent, and a^1 = a.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: For a non-zero number a and integers m and n, a^m × a^n = a^(m + n).
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT Class 7 states this law for whole-number exponents; Class 8 extends it to integer exponents, which is how it is stated here.

knowledge_items.statement: For a non-zero number a and integers m and n, a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m − n).
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT Class 7 states this law for whole-number exponents; Class 8 extends it to integer exponents, which is how it is stated here.

knowledge_items.statement: For a non-zero number a and integers m and n, (a^m)^n = a^(m × n).
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT Class 7 states this law for whole-number exponents; Class 8 extends it to integer exponents, which is how it is stated here.

knowledge_items.statement: For non-zero numbers a and b and an integer m, a^m × b^m = (a × b)^m.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT Class 7 states this law for whole-number exponents; Class 8 extends it to integer exponents, which is how it is stated here.

knowledge_items.statement: For non-zero numbers a and b and an integer m, a^m ÷ b^m = (a ÷ b)^m.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT Class 7 states this law for whole-number exponents; Class 8 extends it to integer exponents, which is how it is stated here.

knowledge_items.statement: For a non-zero number a, a^0 = 1.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Kind has two readings (Concept, as the meaning given to a zero exponent, or Principle, because it follows from a^m ÷ a^m = 1); recorded as Concept. NCERT Class 7 gives it for whole-number bases.

knowledge_items.statement: For a non-zero number a and a positive integer n, a^(−n) = 1 ÷ a^n, so a^(−n) is the reciprocal of a^n.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Kind has two readings (Concept, as the meaning given to a negative exponent, or Principle); recorded as Concept, as for KI-NN-45.

knowledge_items.statement: For non-zero numbers a and b and a positive integer n, (a/b)^(−n) = (b/a)^n.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: A power of a negative number is positive when the exponent is an even integer and negative when the exponent is an odd integer.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT Class 7 states this for positive exponents; Class 8 uses it with negative exponents.

knowledge_items.statement: For a non-zero number a other than 1 and −1, if a^m = a^n for integers m and n, then m = n.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Used without statement in the NCERT Class 8 exercises that ask for an unknown exponent.

knowledge_items.statement: A number is in standard form when it is written as a × 10^n, where 1 ≤ a < 10 and n is an integer.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT Class 7 gives standard form for large numbers (n positive); Class 8 adds small numbers (n negative).

knowledge_items.statement: To write a number in standard form, move the decimal point so that exactly one non-zero digit is before it; the exponent of 10 is the number of places moved, positive when the point moved to the left and negative when it moved to the right.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: Multiplying a number by 10^n moves its decimal point n places to the right when n is positive, and |n| places to the left when n is negative.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: Of two numbers a × 10^n and b × 10^m in standard form, the first is greater when n > m, and when n = m it is greater when a > b.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The quotient of a × 10^n by b × 10^m is (a ÷ b) × 10^(n − m).
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: A variable is a letter that stands for a number that can take different values.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: A number written directly before a letter is multiplied by it, so 3x means 3 × x, x means 1 × x, -x means -1 × x and xy means x × y.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. A convention of algebraic notation.

knowledge_items.statement: An algebraic expression is a combination of numbers and variables joined by operation signs, and it contains no equals sign.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: A term of an algebraic expression is a number, a variable, or a product of numbers and variables, and the terms of an expression are joined by + or − signs.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: In a term, the number that multiplies the variables is the coefficient, and a term with no variable is a constant term.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: Like terms have the same variables raised to the same powers, so 3x²y and −5x²y are like terms but 3x² and 3x are not.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: Like terms are added or subtracted by adding or subtracting their coefficients and keeping the variable part unchanged.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The reason is the distributive property, 3x + 5x = (3 + 5)x.

knowledge_items.statement: Unlike terms cannot be combined into a single term, so a sum of unlike terms such as 3x + 2y stays as two terms.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: To expand a bracket multiplied by a number or a term, multiply every term inside the bracket by that number or term, keeping track of each sign.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: An equation states that two expressions have the same value, and a solution of an equation is a value of the variable that makes the two sides equal.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: Adding or subtracting the same number or term on both sides of an equation, or multiplying or dividing both sides by the same non-zero number, gives an equation with the same solutions.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: A chain of operations is undone by applying the inverse of each operation in the reverse order.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Shared by solving equations, changing the subject of a formula and working backwards through a flowchart. Could also be read as a Principle; see findings.

knowledge_items.statement: Subtracting a number undoes adding that number, and adding a number undoes subtracting it.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Arithmetic item outside AG (cross-domain); the PAL graph holds only the multiplication and division case (KI-RN-27). First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: Multiplying by a non-zero number undoes dividing by that number.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The converse of KI-RN-27 (cross-domain). First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: To solve a linear equation with the variable on both sides, add or subtract a variable term on both sides so that the variable appears on one side only.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: To write an equation for a situation, let a variable stand for one unknown quantity, write the other quantities in terms of it, and set equal two expressions for the same quantity.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The solution of an equation written for a situation answers the question only when it is read as the quantity the variable stands for and fits the conditions of the situation.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The perimeter of a closed shape is the total length of its boundary, measured in units of length.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) LO-G6-17 places perimeter in Grade 6.

knowledge_items.statement: In a decimal, each place has one-tenth the value of the place to its left.
A decimal with n digits after the decimal point is a fraction with denominator 10 to the power n, written in place-value notation.
To add or subtract decimals, line up digits of the same place value, including the decimal points.
Dividing by a non-zero number undoes multiplying by that number.
Division by zero is not defined.
A fraction of a quantity is that fraction multiplied by the quantity.
To multiply two decimals, multiply them as whole numbers and give the product as many decimal places as the two factors have together.
The product or quotient of two rational numbers with the same sign is positive, and with different signs is negative.
The ratio a : b of two quantities of the same kind compares them by division and has no unit.
Multiplying or dividing both terms of a ratio by the same non-zero number gives an equivalent ratio.
The ratio a : b is equal to the fraction a/b, so two ratios are compared by comparing their fractions.
The ratios a : b and c : d are equal exactly when a × d = b × c.
In xⁿ, where n is a positive whole number, x is the base, n is the exponent, and xⁿ is x multiplied by itself n times.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Cross-domain (exponents); the PAL, MYP2 and integers graphs have only the square and cube (KI-NN-01, KI-NN-02).

knowledge_items.statement: When powers of the same base are multiplied, the exponents are added, so xᵐ × xⁿ = xᵐ⁺ⁿ for positive whole numbers m and n.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Cross-domain (exponents). The reason is counting the factors of x.

knowledge_items.statement: To multiply monomials, multiply their numerical coefficients, multiply the powers of each variable by adding the exponents of that variable, and write the results together as one monomial.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: To multiply two polynomials, multiply every term of the first by every term of the second, keeping each sign, and add the products.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The reason is the distributive property applied to each term of the first polynomial in turn. The sum of the products is collected by KI-AG-11 and KI-AG-12.

knowledge_items.statement: An identity is an equation that is true for every value of the variables in it, whereas an equation that is not an identity is true only for some values.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Contrast with an equation (KI-AG-18) is part of the statement.

knowledge_items.statement: For all numbers a and b, (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT shows the reason by multiplying (a + b)(a + b) and by areas.

knowledge_items.statement: For all numbers a and b, (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: For all numbers a and b, (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Read from right to left, it is the factorisation of a difference of two squares; the numerical use in SK-AG-41 is the only right-to-left use in this graph.

knowledge_items.statement: For all numbers x, a and b, (x + a)(x + b) = x² + (a + b)x + ab.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: A two-digit number with tens digit t and units digit u has the value 10t + u, so the number with its digits interchanged has the value 10u + t.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Cross-domain (whole-number place value). Two readings are possible: a Principle, because it states what is true of every two-digit number. Recorded as a Concept because the response is the same form 10t + u in every case. First grade is that of the textbook's digit puzzles; place value of two-digit numbers is taught earlier.

knowledge_items.statement: After k years a person's age is the present age plus k, and k years ago it was the present age minus k, so the ages of two people change by the same number of years.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Two readings are possible: a Fact or term, because the statement is a convention of how ages are counted. Recorded as a Principle because the response changes with the case.

knowledge_items.statement: If two quantities are in the ratio a : b, then they can be written as ax and bx for one number x.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Cross-domain (ratio and proportion); KI-RP-03 gives equivalent ratios but not this converse, and KI-RP-26 gives shares of a total only.

knowledge_items.statement: Consecutive numbers follow one another with the same difference: 1 for consecutive whole numbers, 2 for consecutive even numbers or consecutive odd numbers, and k for consecutive multiples of k.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Learners write consecutive multiples of 8 as n, n + 1 and n + 2 (the separation learner of SK-AG-25). Cross-domain (number patterns); NCERT Grade 8 Chapter 2 uses it in worked examples.

knowledge_items.statement: To solve a linear equation with fractions whose denominators are numbers, multiply every term on both sides by a common multiple of the denominators, so that the equation has no fractions.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: A quadrilateral is a closed figure in a plane bounded by four line segments, and it has four sides, four vertices and four angles.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) places quadrilaterals in Grade 6 (Understanding Elementary Shapes); not checked against the textbook.

knowledge_items.statement: The three angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) places the angle sum of a triangle in Grade 7.

knowledge_items.statement: The four angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The reason is part of the Grade 8 learning: a diagonal splits a convex quadrilateral into two triangles, each with angle sum 180°. The skills in this graph use convex quadrilaterals only.

knowledge_items.statement: An exterior angle of a quadrilateral at a vertex is the angle between one side at that vertex and the extension of the adjacent side, so it and the interior angle at that vertex together make a straight line.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 7 has the exterior angle of a triangle; Grade 8 extends the term to polygons.

knowledge_items.statement: A diagonal of a quadrilateral is a line segment that joins two opposite vertices.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 6 (Understanding Elementary Shapes) defines the diagonal of a polygon; not checked against the textbook.

knowledge_items.statement: A parallelogram is a quadrilateral in which both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 8 (Understanding Quadrilaterals) defines it.

knowledge_items.statement: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The reason (adjacent angles add up to 180°, so each opposite pair is equal) is part of the intended learning for LO-M812.

knowledge_items.statement: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add up to 180°.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The reason (co-interior angles between parallel lines add up to 180°) is part of the intended learning for LO-M812.

knowledge_items.statement: Two line segments bisect each other when they cross at a point that is the midpoint of each.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. First expected grade not checked against a source; Grade 6 Practical Geometry bisects a line segment, but the mutual form is used first in Grade 8.

knowledge_items.statement: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The reason (congruent triangles formed by the diagonals) is part of the intended learning for LO-M812.

knowledge_items.statement: A rhombus is a parallelogram whose four sides are equal in length.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Definition as in NCERT (2017) Grade 8.

knowledge_items.statement: A rectangle is a parallelogram whose four angles are right angles.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Definition as in NCERT (2017) Grade 8, where a rectangle is a parallelogram with equal angles.

knowledge_items.statement: A square is a rectangle whose four sides are equal in length.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Definition as in NCERT (2017) Grade 8.

knowledge_items.statement: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Verified by measuring in Grade 8; the reason is not part of the intended learning.

knowledge_items.statement: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal in length.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Verified by measuring in Grade 8; the reason is not part of the intended learning.

knowledge_items.statement: Every rhombus, every rectangle and every square is a parallelogram, so each has every property of a parallelogram.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The reason is the definitions: a rhombus and a rectangle are each a parallelogram with one extra condition, and a square is a rectangle.

knowledge_items.statement: Every square is both a rectangle and a rhombus.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The reason: a square is a rectangle by definition, and it is a parallelogram with four equal sides, which is a rhombus.

knowledge_items.statement: A parallelogram is a rhombus exactly when two adjacent sides are equal in length, and it is a rectangle exactly when one angle is a right angle.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The reason: opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal, so two equal adjacent sides make all four equal; opposite angles are equal and adjacent angles add up to 180°, so one right angle makes all four right angles.

knowledge_items.statement: A rectangle is a square exactly when two adjacent sides are equal in length, and a rhombus is a square exactly when one angle is a right angle.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The reason follows from the definitions and from the properties of a parallelogram.

knowledge_items.statement: A ruler or a protractor gives a measure only to the nearest division, so two equal lengths or two equal angles can measure slightly differently.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. First expected grade not checked against a source. Sits in measurement more than in geometry.

knowledge_items.statement: Two triangles are congruent when one fits exactly on the other, and then every pair of matching sides and every pair of matching angles are equal.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) places congruence of triangles in Grade 7.

knowledge_items.statement: If two angles and the side between them in one triangle are equal to two angles and the side between them in another triangle, the two triangles are congruent.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. This is the ASA condition of NCERT (2017) Grade 7.

knowledge_items.statement: The front view, the side view and the top view of a solid are the plane figures seen when the solid is looked at from the front, from a side and from above.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) places views of solids in Grade 8 (Visualising Solid Shapes, removed from the textbook in 2023).

knowledge_items.statement: In the top view of a solid made of cubes, there is one square for each stack of cubes, whatever the height of the stack.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The reason is that the top view shows only what is seen from above, which is the top of each stack.

knowledge_items.statement: In the front view or a side view of a solid made of cubes, each position across the view has a column with as many squares as there are cubes in the tallest stack in line with the viewer at that position.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The reason is that the cubes behind the tallest stack in line with the viewer are hidden by it.

knowledge_items.statement: A cuboid standing on one of its faces looks like a rectangle from the front, from the side and from above, and a cube looks like a square from each of these directions.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Stated as one fact about two solids; a reviewer may prefer one item for the cuboid and one for the cube.

knowledge_items.statement: A cylinder standing on its base looks like a rectangle from the front and from the side, and like a circle from above.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: A cone standing on its base looks like a triangle from the front and from the side, and like a circle with a point at its centre for the tip from above.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: A sphere looks like a circle from every direction.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: In the front view and the side view of an object made of one solid standing on the top face of another, the view of the upper solid is drawn above the view of the lower solid, and in the top view the upper solid is drawn over the lower one.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Holds when the upper solid rests within the top face of the lower one, which is the range used in the skills.

knowledge_items.statement: A cuboid is a solid with six rectangular faces.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) LO-G6-15 places cubes and cuboids in Grade 6. KI-GE-20 uses this term without defining it.

knowledge_items.statement: To draw an oblique sketch of a cuboid, draw its front face with its true length and height, draw an equal rectangle for the back face shifted up and to the right, and join the matching corners.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) places oblique sketches in Grade 7 (Visualising Solid Shapes); the chapter was removed from the textbook in 2023.

knowledge_items.statement: To draw an isometric sketch of a cuboid on isometric dot paper, draw its edges along the vertical dot lines and the two sets of slanting dot lines, each edge as many dot spaces long as the number of units in its length.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) places isometric sketches in Grade 7 (Visualising Solid Shapes); the chapter was removed from the textbook in 2023.

knowledge_items.statement: A polyhedron is a solid whose surface is made only of flat polygons.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 8 (Visualising Solid Shapes, removed from the textbook in 2023) defines it.

knowledge_items.statement: A face of a polyhedron is one of the flat polygons that make up its surface.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: An edge of a polyhedron is a line segment where two of its faces meet.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: A vertex of a polyhedron is a point where three or more of its edges meet.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: A prism is a polyhedron that has two identical polygons in parallel planes as its bases and rectangles as its other faces.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Stated for right prisms, which are the prisms of the textbook; first expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: A pyramid is a polyhedron that has a polygon as its base and triangles as its other faces, all meeting at one vertex.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: A polygon with five sides is a pentagon and a polygon with six sides is a hexagon.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) places polygons in Grade 6.

knowledge_items.statement: For every polyhedron, the number of faces F, the number of vertices V and the number of edges E satisfy F + V − E = 2.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Euler's relation as in NCERT (2017) Grade 8 (Visualising Solid Shapes, removed from the textbook in 2023). The textbook checks it on a table of solids; a proof is not part of the learning.

knowledge_items.statement: A pair of compasses set to a length r draws a circle or an arc whose radius is r.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 6 (Practical Geometry) introduces compasses.

knowledge_items.statement: A point at distance r from a point P and at distance s from a point Q lies on the circle with centre P and radius r and on the circle with centre Q and radius s, so it is a point where the two circles meet.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. This is the reason behind the arc method used in every construction in this graph.

knowledge_items.statement: To construct a triangle from its three sides, draw one side as the base, draw arcs from its two end points with radii equal to the other two sides, and join the point where the arcs meet to the two end points.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) places construction of triangles in Grade 7.

knowledge_items.statement: Four sides do not fix a quadrilateral, because the same four sides can be joined to give quadrilaterals of different shapes, so a fifth measurement such as a diagonal or an angle is needed.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 8 (Practical Geometry, removed from the textbook in 2023) gives this as the reason a diagonal or an angle is added.

knowledge_items.statement: A diagonal of a quadrilateral divides it into two triangles.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Two readings of kind: principle, or concept because the result is always two triangles; recorded as a principle.

knowledge_items.statement: To draw an angle of a given measure at a point on a line with a protractor, place the centre of the protractor on the point and its base line along the line, mark the given measure on the scale, and draw the ray from the point through the mark.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 6 (Understanding Elementary Shapes) measures and draws angles with a protractor.

knowledge_items.statement: To construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment, draw from each end point an arc of the same radius, longer than half the segment, so that the arcs cross on both sides of the segment, and join the two crossing points.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 6 (Practical Geometry).

knowledge_items.statement: To construct a perpendicular to a line at a point on it, mark two points on the line at equal distances from that point, draw from each an arc of the same larger radius so that the arcs cross, and join the crossing point to the given point.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 6 (Practical Geometry).

knowledge_items.statement: To construct a quadrilateral ABCD from sides AB, BC, CD and DA and diagonal AC, construct triangle ABC from AB, BC and AC, then construct triangle ACD from AC, CD and DA on the other side of AC.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 8 (Practical Geometry, removed from the textbook in 2023).

knowledge_items.statement: To construct a quadrilateral ABCD from sides AB, BC and CD and diagonals AC and BD, construct triangle ABC from AB, BC and AC, then mark D as the point at distance CD from C and at distance BD from B.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 8 (Practical Geometry, removed from the textbook in 2023).

knowledge_items.statement: To construct a quadrilateral ABCD from sides AB and BC and angles A, B and C, draw AB, draw angle B at B and mark C on its arm at distance BC, draw angle A at A and angle C at C, and mark D where the other arms of these two angles meet.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 8 (Practical Geometry, removed from the textbook in 2023).

knowledge_items.statement: To construct a quadrilateral ABCD from sides AB, BC and CD and angles B and C, draw BC, draw angle B at B and mark A on its arm at distance AB, draw angle C at C and mark D on its arm at distance CD, then join A and D.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 8 (Practical Geometry, removed from the textbook in 2023).

knowledge_items.statement: To construct a parallelogram ABCD from sides AB and AD and angle A, draw AB, draw angle A at A and mark D on its arm at distance AD, then mark C as the point at distance AD from B and at distance AB from D.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The step that finds C uses the equality of opposite sides (KI-GE-13). NCERT (2017) Grade 8 (Practical Geometry, removed from the textbook in 2023).

knowledge_items.statement: To construct a rhombus ABCD from diagonals AC and BD, draw AC, construct its perpendicular bisector, mark B and D on the bisector on the two sides of AC at distance half of BD from the midpoint of AC, and join A, B, C and D.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 8 (Practical Geometry, removed from the textbook in 2023).

knowledge_items.statement: To construct a rectangle ABCD from sides AB and BC, draw AB, construct perpendiculars to AB at A and at B, mark D on the perpendicular at A and C on the perpendicular at B, each at distance BC from AB on the same side of AB, and join C and D; when AB equals BC the rectangle is a square.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) Grade 8 (Practical Geometry, removed from the textbook in 2023).

knowledge_items.statement: A transversal is a line that crosses two or more lines at different points.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: Parallel lines are lines in the same plane that never meet, however far they are extended.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: Alternate interior angles are a pair of angles, one at each point where a transversal crosses two lines, that lie between the two lines and on opposite sides of the transversal.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The topic hint says alternate (interior); alternate exterior angles are not included.

knowledge_items.statement: Co-interior angles are a pair of angles, one at each point where a transversal crosses two lines, that lie between the two lines and on the same side of the transversal.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) calls these interior angles on the same side of the transversal.

knowledge_items.statement: When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, each pair of alternate interior angles is equal.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, each pair of co-interior angles adds up to 180°.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: Adjacent angles that together make a straight line add up to 180°.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) M711 places linear pairs in Grade 7.

knowledge_items.statement: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal in length.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Classified as a principle (it holds for every parallelogram and the lengths change); a reader could take it as a fact about one shape. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: A cube is a cuboid whose length, width and height are equal.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) LO-G6-15 places cubes and cuboids in Grade 6.

knowledge_items.statement: The radius of a circle is the distance from its centre to any point on the circle, and its diameter, a chord through the centre, is twice the radius.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: When a quantity is divided in a given ratio, each share is the quantity multiplied by that share's term divided by the sum of the terms.
knowledge_items.note: Two readings of kind: as a statement of what each share is (principle) or as the steps divide by the sum of the terms, then multiply (procedure); recorded as principle.

knowledge_items.statement: The area of a shape is the amount of surface it covers, measured in square units, where 1 cm² is the area of a square with sides of 1 cm and 1 m² is the area of a square with sides of 1 m.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. NCERT (2017) LO-G6-17 places area in Grade 6.

knowledge_items.statement: The area of a rectangle is its length multiplied by its width.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Needed inside compound shapes; the MYP2 topic lines do not list rectangles, the Unit 4 summative does.

knowledge_items.statement: The perpendicular height of a triangle, parallelogram or trapezium is the length of the segment that meets the base, or the line containing the base, at a right angle and reaches the opposite vertex or side.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The area of a parallelogram is its base multiplied by its perpendicular height.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The area of a triangle is half of its base multiplied by its perpendicular height.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The area of a trapezium is half the sum of its two parallel sides multiplied by the perpendicular distance between them.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. MYP2 expects it in Grade 7; NCERT (2017) places the area of a trapezium in Grade 8 (M816).

knowledge_items.statement: The circumference of every circle is π times its diameter, or 2π times its radius, where π is a fixed number approximately equal to 3.14 or 22/7.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The area of a circle with radius r is π × r².
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The area of a shape made of parts that do not overlap is the sum of the areas of the parts.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: The volume of a solid is the amount of space it occupies, measured in cubic units, where 1 cm³ is the volume of a cube with edges of 1 cm and 1 m³ is the volume of a cube with edges of 1 m.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. MYP2 expects it in Grade 7; NCERT (2017) places volume of a cuboid in Grade 8 (M818).

knowledge_items.statement: The volume of a cuboid is its length multiplied by its width multiplied by its height.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. MYP2 expects it in Grade 7; NCERT (2017) places it in Grade 8 (M818).

knowledge_items.statement: The surface area of a solid is the total area of all its faces.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: A cuboid with length l, width w and height h has six rectangular faces in three pairs of equal opposite faces, so its total surface area is 2(lw + wh + lh).
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. MYP2 expects it in Grade 7; NCERT (2017) places it in Grade 8 (M818).

knowledge_items.statement: A situation about filling the inside of a solid, such as filling a tank or packing a box, calls for its volume, and a situation about covering its outside, such as painting or wrapping, calls for its surface area.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: An area or a volume is found from lengths only after all the lengths are written in the same unit.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Worded on the model of KI-RP-02 and classified the same way; it could also be read as a principle. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: To estimate the area of a shape drawn on a square grid, count each full square and each square covered by more than half as 1, count each square covered by half as one half, leave out each square covered by less than half, and add; the total is the area in square units.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The counting convention is read from the NCERT mensuration chapters; a reviewer should confirm it against the textbook. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: An area found by counting squares on a grid is an estimate, close to but usually not equal to the area found by a formula, because the part squares are judged by eye.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: The area of a quadrilateral with a diagonal of length d, and perpendiculars of lengths h1 and h2 drawn to the diagonal from the other two vertices, is 1/2 × d × (h1 + h2).
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The area of a rhombus with diagonals of lengths d1 and d2 is 1/2 × d1 × d2.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: To find the area of a polygon, split it into triangles and trapeziums by drawing diagonals and perpendiculars, find the area of each piece, and add the areas of the pieces.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The lateral surface area of a cuboid, a cube or a cylinder is the area of its surface other than its top and bottom, which is the curved surface for a cylinder, and its total surface area is its lateral surface area plus the areas of its top and bottom.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The lateral surface area of a cuboid with length l, width w and height h is 2h(l + w), the perimeter of its base multiplied by its height.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. The cube is the case with l = w = h, through KI-GE-20; no separate cube item is written.

knowledge_items.statement: A cylinder is a solid whose two ends are equal circles in parallel planes, joined by a curved surface; its radius is the radius of an end and its height is the distance between the ends.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: The curved surface area of a cylinder with base radius r and height h is 2πrh, because the curved surface opens out into a rectangle as long as the circumference of the base and as wide as the height.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The total surface area of a cylinder with base radius r and height h is 2πrh + 2πr², which is 2πr(r + h): its curved surface area plus the areas of its two circular ends.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The volume of a cylinder with base radius r and height h is πr²h, the area of its base multiplied by its height.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: The capacity of a container is the volume of liquid it holds when full, measured in litres or millilitres.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: One litre is 1000 cubic centimetres.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: One cubic metre is 1 000 000 cubic centimetres.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026.

knowledge_items.statement: One cubic metre is 1000 litres.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Follows from KI-ME-37 and KI-ME-38 but is stated as a fact in the NCERT chapter, so it is kept as its own item.

knowledge_items.statement: A diagonal of a polygon is a line segment that joins two vertices that are not next to each other.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Geometry term needed inside mensuration; listed under cross_domain_kis. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: A rhombus is a quadrilateral whose four sides are equal in length.
knowledge_items.note: authored by ConveGenius, 24 Oct 2026. Geometry term needed inside mensuration; listed under cross_domain_kis. First expected grade not checked against a source.

knowledge_items.statement: One metre is 100 centimetres.
An amount in a smaller unit is written as a decimal of the larger unit by dividing it by the number of smaller units in one larger unit.
A situation of equal groups or scaling is represented by multiplication, and a situation of sharing or measuring is represented by division.
In the unitary method, the value of one unit is the value of a given number of units divided by that number, and the value of any number of units is that number times the value of one unit.
R percent of a quantity Q is Q multiplied by R/100.
On a scale along a graph axis, equal distances stand for equal differences in value.
The probability of an event is a number from 0 to 1, and the greater the probability, the more likely the event is to happen.
An experiment is an action whose result is uncertain, each possible result is an outcome, and the sample space is the set of all possible outcomes.
An event is a set of outcomes from the sample space, and it happens when the result of the experiment is one of those outcomes.
Outcomes are equally likely when each has the same chance of happening, as for a fair coin, a fair die or a counter taken at random from a bag.
When all the outcomes of an experiment are equally likely, the theoretical probability of an event is the number of outcomes in the event divided by the total number of outcomes.
knowledge_items.note: Two kind readings: Principle (states what is true under equal likelihood) or Procedure (count and divide); Principle chosen, gate before attainment.

knowledge_items.statement: The probability that an event does not happen is 1 minus the probability that it happens.
The experimental probability of an event is the number of trials in which the event happens divided by the total number of trials.
knowledge_items.note: Also called relative frequency. Kind: a definition, classed as Concept like the mean (KI-DA-06); a Principle reading is possible.

knowledge_items.statement: As the number of trials increases, the experimental probability of an event tends to come closer to its theoretical probability.
A bar graph shows each category of a data set as a bar of the same width, with equal gaps between bars, and the length of a bar on a scale stands for the frequency or amount of that category.
A double bar graph shows two data sets for the same categories by drawing, for each category, two bars side by side in different shades, with a key that tells which shade stands for which data set.

To choose a scale for the axis of a bar graph, divide the length of the axis into equal divisions that each stand for a convenient number of units, such as 1, 2, 5, 10 or 100, so that the greatest value fits on the axis.
knowledge_items.note: Two kind readings: Procedure (choose, then check that the greatest value fits) or Principle (a scale is usable when its divisions are equal and the greatest value fits); Procedure chosen, gate before attainment.

knowledge_items.statement: A pie chart is a circle divided into sectors by radii, in which the whole circle stands for the total of the data and each sector shows the share of one category, with a central angle proportional to that share.
knowledge_items.note: Also called a circle graph in the NCERT Class 8 chapter.

knowledge_items.statement: To find the central angle of a sector of a pie chart, write the value of its category as a fraction of the total of the data, or its percentage as a fraction of 100, and multiply that fraction by 360°.
A full turn about a point, such as the centre of a circle, is 360°, so the angles between radii that together fill a circle add up to 360°.
knowledge_items.note: Geometry fact needed by pie charts; listed under cross_domain_kis.

knowledge_items.statement: To draw an angle of a given size with a protractor, place the centre of the protractor on the vertex and its zero line along one arm, mark the given size on the scale, and join the mark to the vertex.
knowledge_items.note: Geometry procedure needed by pie charts; listed under cross_domain_kis.

knowledge_items.statement: To draw a pie chart, draw a circle and one radius, then draw each sector's central angle in turn from the radius that ends the sector before it, so that the sectors fill the circle without overlapping.
A sector of a pie chart with a central angle of x degrees shows x/360 of the total of the data, which is x/360 × 100 percent of it.

To read the value of a bar, follow from the top of the bar across to the scale and read the value there; when the top lies between two marked divisions, use the equal parts between them to find the value.
A trial is one performance of an experiment, such as one toss of a coin or one throw of a die, and an event happens in a trial when the result is one of the outcomes of the event.
knowledge_items.note: The Class 8 chapter speaks of tossing a coin or throwing a die a number of times; the word trial is used in the Class 9 chapter. Replaces the simulation wording of MYP2 KI-PR-16, which is not copied.

knowledge_items.statement: When an experiment is repeated in the same way, the experimental probability of an event from earlier trials is an estimate of the probability that the event happens in a further trial, and the estimate is better the more earlier trials there are.
knowledge_items.note: Authored for the reading of M820 used here (a hypothesis about a future event from earlier occurrences); the Class 8 chapter does not state it in these words.

knowledge_items.statement: In n trials of an experiment, an event with probability p is expected to happen about n × p times.
knowledge_items.note: Authored for the reading of M820 used here; the Class 8 chapter does not state it in these words. The probability p may be experimental or theoretical.

knowledge_items.statement: In repeated trials of an experiment with equally likely outcomes, the number of times an event happens is usually close to, but seldom exactly equal to, the number of trials times the theoretical probability of the event.
knowledge_items.note: Authored for the reading of M820 used here; the Class 8 chapter does not state it in these words.

findings.NN:
- Reading used for M803 ("Proves divisibility rules of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 11"): the task is giving the justification for a stated rule, in words or letters, for a number of two or three digits, from the generalised form 10a + b or 100a + 10b + c. Five justification skills are grouped by the form of the argument: the units digit (rules of 2 and 5, SK-NN-06), the last two digits (rule of 4, SK-NN-07), the digit sum (rules of 3 and 9, SK-NN-08), the alternating sum (rule of 11, SK-NN-09), and the combination of two rules (rule of 6 from the divisibility by 2 and by 3, SK-NN-10). Writing the number in generalised form is the one step (SK-NN-11), always part of SK-NN-06 to 09 because the tasks give the digits and not the form. The SLOF note says the chapter (Playing with Numbers) was removed from the Class 8 textbook in the 2023 rationalisation; the scope here is taken from the earlier Class 8 chapter and the Class 6 chapter that states the tests.
- Left out of M803: applying a rule to decide whether a given number is divisible (the outcome says proves, and no justification needs it); puzzles in which letters stand for digits and the "reversing the digits" problems with 10b + a; the rules for 8 and 10, which the chapter teaches but the outcome does not list; justifications for numbers of four or more digits.
- Reading used for M804 ("Finds squares, cubes and square roots and cube roots of numbers using different methods"): the method is a condition, so methods that give different task types are separate skills. Squares and cubes are found by multiplication (SK-NN-13 and the copied SK-NN-02). Square roots have three methods, each a skill: prime factorisation (SK-NN-18), repeated subtraction of odd numbers (SK-NN-19) and the division method, which has three task types (perfect squares SK-NN-20, decimals SK-NN-21, whole numbers that are not perfect squares to one decimal place SK-NN-22). Cube roots have one method in the chapter, prime factorisation (SK-NN-23). The estimate of a root to one decimal place is read as the end of the division method (SK-NN-22).
- Judgment call in M804: deciding whether a number is a perfect square or cube (SK-NN-14, SK-NN-15) and finding the smallest multiplier or divisor that makes one (SK-NN-16, SK-NN-17) are written as outcome tasks because the scope guidance lists them, but the outcome asks for finding squares, cubes and roots; they trace to the outcome only through the phrase "using different methods" and through the chapter tasks that take a root of the product after finding the multiplier. A reviewer who reads the outcome strictly can remove these four skills and their knowledge items (KI-NN-27, 28, 36, 37).
- Left out of M804: squares and cubes of decimals, fractions and numbers of more than three digits; squares by the identity (a + b)² (algebraic identities belong to another outcome); properties and patterns of squares and cubes (units digits, number of zeros, number of digits in a root, numbers between consecutive squares, triangular numbers, sums of odd numbers as a pattern, 1729 and sums of two cubes); Pythagorean triplets (the outcome asks for finding squares and roots, and the triplet rule m² − 1, 2m, m² + 1 is a property of squares used for a different task); square roots of fractions and cube roots of negative numbers, decimals and fractions; the least number to be added to or subtracted from a number to make a perfect square; word problems that use squares and roots, such as the side of a square park or the rows of an arrangement.
- Reading used for M805 ("Solves problems with integral exponents"): the outcome tasks are problems and simplifications that use the laws, so bare evaluation of one power is a step (SK-NN-24), always part of SK-NN-27 and sometimes part of SK-NN-25, SK-NN-26 and SK-NN-30 (in SK-NN-30 only when the exponent is negative). The outcome tasks are: simplifying powers of one base (SK-NN-25), simplifying powers of different bases with the same exponent (SK-NN-26), evaluating an expression with negative exponents (SK-NN-27), finding an unknown exponent (SK-NN-28), writing a number in standard form and in usual form (SK-NN-29, SK-NN-30), comparing numbers in standard form (SK-NN-31) and finding how many times one quantity is as large as another (SK-NN-32). Standard form and comparison are included because the scope guidance places them in this outcome; the outcome text does not mention them. Recall of the laws is recorded as knowledge items (KI-NN-40 to 49).

findings.PR:
- Reading used for M820: SLOF maps the outcome to a curricular goal about the history of mathematics, which looks wrong; the outcome and the Class 8 chapter Data Handling (chance and probability) are about the chance of an event, so this graph uses the outcome text. 'Makes hypotheses on chances of future events on the basis of earlier occurrences or available data' is read as stating, from recorded results of repeated trials, the chance of an event in a further trial (SK-PR-09), predicting how many times it will happen in a stated number of further trials (SK-PR-10), and judging whether a recorded result is as expected for equally likely outcomes (SK-PR-11).
- SK-PR-10 and SK-PR-11 follow the scope note given with the task rather than words in the NCERT chapter: the chapter does not state the expected number n × p (KI-PR-21) or that recorded counts are near but seldom equal to expected counts (KI-PR-22). The NCERT text for these items is not confirmed; a reviewer should decide whether SK-PR-10 and SK-PR-11 belong to M820. SK-PR-11 has no threshold for 'close' in NCERT; the conditions set a clearly close or clearly far record.
